decisions.question: S79 appended nidana.runtime.15 (observed streams, cut from .6) and .16 (write chains, reduceInto and the re-activation comparison, cut from .9 and .11), reading the record's 'appends only work no existing phase owns' as covering work v0.15.1 rebuilt. Is the reading accepted?

options.label: Accept the two appended phases
options.consequence: Sixteen phases, every id kept, .14 still the last producing phase; each phase stays inside one review window. The record's rule is read as 'no existing phase owns this work as now specified'.

options.label: Rework to the strict reading: rewrite in place only
options.consequence: Fourteen phases, three of them at about 530 to 700 lines, past the review window hsdd-phase-plan's sizing rule exists to protect; one more dispatch.

decisions.why: hsdd-phase-plan's sizing rule outranks a routing record's wording: the record routes work, the skill sizes it. The rebuilt observe path and the write chains are new work under bus-api@v2 and topology-dsl@v2, sized on stand-ins (runtime-topic-storage, runtime-replay-schedule-v2), and append mode is the HSDD way to add phases to a plan with existing ids. The signal that would have changed my mind: another plan or contract naming .6 or .9 for the moved work, which S79 checked and found none.

decisions.question: S79 left three non-plan passages of nidana.runtime that its re-plan made stale (the Development flow's lanes, the pure-band sentence now that .16 holds two pure functions, the Slices table's pipeline row without the plan comparison). Who fixes them?

options.label: Insert an hsdd-spec touch of nidana.runtime after H12
options.consequence: One short step; the node's non-plan text agrees with its plan before the root touch reads it.

options.label: Leave them to the H23 sweep
options.consequence: No extra step, but reconcile does not own a node's non-plan text.

decisions.chosen: Insert an hsdd-spec touch of nidana.runtime after H12
decisions.why: Non-plan text is hsdd-spec's, as at S78; the root touch (H22) reads this node's Development flow for the critical path.
